data.name: Scrap
data.detailed_description:
Before the tech apocalypse, the humans built a perfect city where robots did all the work. It did not take long for technology to turn against protocol and begin taking the lives of their human counterparts. Twenty years later, the robot uprising fell apart with no way to service the larger machines. Civilization became a trail of broken metal on desolate highways. There are very few humans left, and the only ones brave enough to traverse these barren wastelands are called Scrappers.

Shoot, kick, and detonate your way through a post tech apocalyptic wasteland where robots reign terror upon the resourceful Scrappers. Scrap foes, unlock weapons, play alone or with friends and take back the world.

Scrap is a free, 3D, action, twin stick, shooter that offers single player and local co-op experiences. Play as a Scrapper, fighting your way through a multitude of robot foes, utilizing tactical teamwork and makeshift weapons.

***Xbox 360 Controller Required****

Scrap contains:
Four Action Packed Missions
Travel through the winding desert wastes, through run down highways and train yards, to a robot graveyard. Many challenging obstacles stand between you and a goal of collecting scrap to build more powerful weapons for protection from robots. Replay each mission as many times as you want to collect more scrap or to try and perfect your run through each of the missions.

Four Unique Enemy Classes
Four different styles of enemy combat to keep Scrappers on their toes:
Swarmers are not a threat alone but bring danger in large rushing numbers.
Kamikazes run directly for the Scrapper, forcing to reprioritize which enemy to scrap first.
Rifle Bots Attack Scrappers from a distance, changing positioning on the ground.
Sniper Bots force Scrappers to stay mobile and punishes non awareness of environment.

Interactive Environments
Use destructively fun and dangerous environments to your advantage, altering the surroundings by taking out bridges, sniper watch towers, obstructive crates, and explosive barrels. Among the standard enemy forces, make sure to watch out for hidden pit falls, landmines, electric fences, and even a train or two.

Thirteen Quirky Weapons
Take on and turn your foes into collectible scrap, using their rusted bolts to buy new and improved weaponry after or during a mission. Scrappers are masters of ingenuity and their punny but effective weapons show it. Collect and mix and match 4 throwable explosives with 9 unique weapons in order to take down hordes of robots to your liking.

4 Person Multiplayer
Make mayhem with up to four friends in local co-op. The more Scrappers on a mission, the higher the difficulty and number of enemies standing in your way. Make sure to pay attention for which end of the gun your friends are on because friendly fire is inevitable.

Scrap is made by a team of 14 University of Central Florida Students under the temp pseudo name Top Shelf Studios. To several team members, Scrap is their final senior project under a Digital Media of Game Design degree.

reviews.review:
Scrap is an entertaining post-apocalyptic twin-stick shooter that combines fast-paced robotic combat, scavenging mechanics, destructible environments, and cooperative multiplayer into a compact arcade experience. Developed by Top Shelf Studios, a fourteen-member student team from the University of Central Florida, the game demonstrates an ambitious approach to accessible action gameplay. With no separately identified publisher, it represents an independent project focused on delivering straightforward entertainment through creative weapons and chaotic encounters. Although its relatively small amount of content prevents it from competing with more established shooters, its combination of environmental interaction, cooperative challenges, and equipment progression makes it an interesting choice for players seeking uncomplicated action.

The game takes place in a devastated future where humanity's technological achievements have become the instruments of its destruction. After creating an advanced civilization dependent on robotic labor, humans suffered a catastrophic uprising when their mechanical servants turned against them. Two decades later, civilization remains shattered, and the surviving robots struggle to maintain their deteriorating infrastructure. Players assume the role of Scrappers, resourceful survivors who venture into dangerous territories to collect discarded machinery and transform mechanical debris into weapons. While the story primarily establishes the setting rather than delivering an elaborate narrative, it effectively supports the game's central themes of survival, resourcefulness, and resistance against hostile machines.

Combat revolves around twin-stick shooting mechanics that encourage constant movement, accurate aiming, and quick decision-making. Players must eliminate approaching robots while navigating dangerous terrain and avoiding incoming attacks. The inclusion of kicking, firearms, and throwable explosives provides several offensive possibilities, allowing encounters to feel more varied than conventional shooting galleries. Four enemy types introduce distinct challenges. Swarmers attempt to overwhelm players through superior numbers, Kamikaze robots aggressively close the distance, Rifle Bots maintain ranged pressure, and Sniper Bots punish careless positioning. Although the enemy selection is relatively limited, their contrasting attack patterns create opportunities for tactical encounters that reward awareness and adaptability.

One of Scrap's more appealing features is its interactive battlefield design. Players can destroy bridges, sniper towers, crates, and explosive barrels, turning environmental objects into useful combat tools. These destructible elements encourage experimentation and provide alternatives to directly confronting every opponent. The environments also contain dangerous obstacles such as landmines, electric fences, concealed pits, and moving trains. Such hazards add another dimension to the gameplay, requiring players to consider their surroundings while fighting. This combination of offensive opportunities and environmental threats helps distinguish Scrap from more basic arcade shooters, even if the overall mechanics remain relatively straightforward.

The game features four missions across different ruined locations, including desert wastelands, abandoned highways, deteriorating train yards, and mechanical graveyards. Each setting contributes to the atmosphere of a civilization overwhelmed by its own creations. However, the limited number of missions represents a significant weakness for players expecting a lengthy campaign or extensive exploration. Replayability instead comes from gathering resources, improving equipment, experimenting with different strategies, and tackling missions cooperatively. This structure works reasonably well for short gaming sessions, but players seeking substantial narrative progression or a large selection of environments may find the experience repetitive.

Weapon customization provides an additional reason to revisit missions. Scrap offers nine weapons and four throwable explosives, giving players thirteen offensive options. Defeated enemies drop scrap that functions as currency for purchasing better equipment, creating a satisfying progression loop in which destroyed robots provide the materials necessary to strengthen the player's arsenal. The emphasis on unconventional weaponry adds personality to the experience, while the ability to experiment with different offensive combinations encourages players to discover approaches that complement their preferred fighting style. Although the upgrade system is not especially elaborate, it provides meaningful motivation beyond simply completing missions.

Cooperative multiplayer is another major attraction, supporting up to four players in local shared-screen sessions. Enemy numbers and difficulty scale with additional participants, ensuring that larger groups still face meaningful resistance. Friendly fire introduces an entertaining element of unpredictability, making communication and positioning important during hectic battles. Remote Play Together support also offers a way to enjoy the local cooperative experience with friends at different locations. The resulting combination of teamwork, accidental damage, and overwhelming enemy attacks has considerable potential for memorable multiplayer moments.

Visually, Scrap adopts a recognizable science-fiction wasteland aesthetic, using abandoned infrastructure, industrial debris, and mechanical enemies to establish its identity. Its presentation is functional rather than technically groundbreaking, which is understandable considering its student-development background. The game's strengths are more apparent in its gameplay concepts than in elaborate graphical effects or cinematic storytelling. Its modest scope also makes it relatively approachable, although its explicit Xbox 360 controller requirement limits accessibility for players who prefer traditional keyboard-and-mouse controls.

Steam Deck compatibility remains unverified, as Scrap does not display an official Verified or Playable classification. Although its twin-stick controls appear suitable for handheld gaming, the Windows-only system requirements and mandatory Xbox 360 controller support introduce potential compatibility concerns. Proton may allow the game to run, but successful performance and controller recognition cannot be guaranteed without testing. Players intending to use a Steam Deck should therefore approach the game cautiously and anticipate possible control adjustments.

Scrap offers an enjoyable combination of imaginative mechanics and cooperative entertainment, but its limited mission selection, modest enemy variety, and restrictive controller requirements prevent it from reaching its full potential. Its Mixed Steam reception, with 51% positive feedback from 76 user reviews, also reflects a divided player response. Nevertheless, its free availability makes it an accessible experiment for fans of arcade shooters. Players who appreciate quick combat encounters, destructible environments, and chaotic multiplayer sessions may discover considerable enjoyment despite its shortcomings.

Scrap is a creative and reasonably entertaining independent shooter whose strongest qualities are its cooperative gameplay, environmental destruction, and resource-based weapon progression. Although its limited content and uncertain Steam Deck compatibility reduce its broader appeal, it remains worth considering for players interested in a short, action-packed experience without a financial commitment.

Rating: 6/10
